title: Space from the description language Ilanguage 1.b
summary: Studies whether a space-like structure can be derived inside the description language Ilanguage 1.b from the language's own elements, without importing any spatial notion. It asks which features a later study of gravity needs follow, and under which conditions: points, distance, locality, dimension, bodies, motion, localized cost and state-dependent geometry.

success_criteria.name: Points
success_criteria.text: The entities that carry the space are defined from Ilanguage elements, without labels.

success_criteria.name: Neighbourhood and locality
success_criteria.text: There is a notion of near points consistent with the distance, and it is settled whether the contract system couples only near points.

success_criteria.name: Paths
success_criteria.text: Betweenness and shortest paths (geodesics) are determined in the derived space.

success_criteria.name: Dimension
success_criteria.text: A notion of dimension is given, with the conditions that fix its value and the conditions under which families of growing size give a continuum-like space.

success_criteria.name: Body
success_criteria.text: A body is localized in the derived space, persists under the evolution and is specified without labels; it has a position, and two bodies have a distance.

success_criteria.name: Background
success_criteria.text: The points of the spaces obtained at different λ are identified, with the conditions for a stable background, so that a body has a trajectory.

success_criteria.name: Time
success_criteria.text: Handed over to the time project: this subproject derives no clock, and its rates are rates with respect to λ.

success_criteria.name: Velocity and acceleration
success_criteria.text: The rate of change of a body's position with respect to λ is determined, together with whether the contract system implies a maximal propagation speed and the velocities relative to it.

success_criteria.name: Localized cost
success_criteria.text: The distribution of the cost over the derived space is determined, and the cost of a body is studied as the analogue of mass.

success_criteria.name: State-dependent geometry
success_criteria.text: It is determined how the distance and the curvature change with the state.

success_criteria.name: Common space
success_criteria.text: It is determined how the spaces derived from the views of different parts fit together: when they coincide, and otherwise which rule relates them.
